courses.name: First Year Seminar
courses.description: Supports university transition, community connections and student planning.

category_review.locator: CS 1200 course block; description, not department or degree label

courses.name: Journalism at Northeastern
courses.description: Introduces journalism students to liberal arts study, academic skills and the university community.

category_review.locator: JRNL 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description concerns first-year orientation, academic/interpersonal skills and university community values, not substantive journalism methods.

courses.name: First-Year Interdisciplinary Seminar
courses.description: Explores global citizenship, university resources and interdisciplinary problem solving.

category_review.locator: INPR 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The first-year seminar emphasizes university resources and personal/academic development with global-challenge context, without a sufficiently specified substantive subject for this taxonomy.

courses.name: Professional Development for Khoury Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op applications, interviews and workplace expectations.

category_review.locator: CS 1210 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Co-op preparation, resumes, interviews and workplace conduct do not establish a primary computing subject category.

courses.name: Professional Development for Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op searches, interviewing, professional practice and career decisions.

category_review.locator: EEAM 2000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course prepares students for co-op searches, professional behavior and career choices rather than a substantive discipline-method curriculum.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

category_review.locator: CS 1800 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sets, relations, induction, proof, logic and counting form discrete mathematical methods; computing motivates their use.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

category_review.locator: CS 2000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2001 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.

category_review.locator: CS 2100 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2101 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: The Law, Ethics, and Policy of Data and Digital Technologies
courses.description: Examines legal and ethical rules governing digital data, privacy and automated systems.

category_review.locator: CY 4170 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description centers on legal rights, data ethics, privacy and the social impact of information practices, not security implementation.

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3500 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: DS 4400 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

courses.name: Advanced Machine Learning
courses.description: Studies advanced learning methods and their mathematical and computational foundations.
courses.prerequisites: DS 4400 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4420 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Advanced learning algorithms, structured-data models, Bayesian estimation and generative models are explicitly machine-learning content.

courses.name: Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics
courses.description: Combines digital design, programming and embedded systems to control robotic devices.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2140 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: EECE 2160 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description integrates digital hardware design, object-oriented programming/Linux and a robotic-device project without establishing one dominant subject among systems, programming and domain implementation. The robotics example does not establish an AI-method course.

courses.name: Fundamentals of Digital Design and Computer Organization
courses.description: Develops digital logic, computer architecture and hardware models for a simple processor.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2160 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2310 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: EECE 2322 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Logic circuits, instruction-set architecture, processor construction, hardware-description languages and assembly interfaces establish computer architecture/digital systems as the primary subject.

courses.name: Lab for EECE 2322
courses.description: Designs, simulates and tests a computer system using programmable logic.

category_review.locator: EECE 2323 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The laboratory designs, implements, simulates and tests a computer system on programmable logic using a hardware-description language.

courses.name: Digital, Analytics, Technology, and Automation Research Practicum
courses.description: Applies analytics, digital technology and machine learning to client problems through a research practicum.

category_review.locator: MKTG 4606 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The practicum centers on solving client business/organizational problems with digital technology and analytics, combining technical and managerial practice. Machine learning is one stated tool, not evidence that a fixed AI algorithm curriculum dominates every project.

courses.name: Journalism 1: Fundamentals of Reporting and Writing
courses.description: Introduces news reporting and writing through interviews, observation, research and critical analysis.

category_review.locator: JRNL 1101 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Reporting, newswriting, interviewing, attribution and analysis of media institutions establish communication and social analysis as the subject.

courses.name: Journalist’s Toolbox
courses.description: Introduces photographic, audio, video and data-visualization tools for journalistic storytelling.

category_review.locator: JRNL 1102 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Photo/audio/video and visualization tools are taught explicitly for journalistic storytelling; operating editing software is not general software construction.

courses.name: Journalism 2: Intermediate Reporting
courses.description: Develops intermediate reporting through interviews, background research, public records, story organization and online presentation.
courses.prerequisites: JRNL 1101 with a minimum grade of C or COMM 238M with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: JRNL 2201 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Reporting, interviewing, public-record research and organization of online news stories are the primary communication skills.

courses.name: Visual Storytelling in Journalism
courses.description: Practices journalistic storytelling with audio, video and still images for presentation across formats.

category_review.locator: JRNL 2301 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course teaches journalistic storytelling through audio, video and images across presentation formats.

courses.name: Digital Storytelling and Social Media
courses.description: Creates digital stories and coordinated cross-platform campaigns for varied audiences, informed by online storytelling and social-media history.

category_review.locator: JRNL 3610 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Digital stories, audience-specific communication and strategic media campaigns are the substantive focus, with technology serving those communication goals.

courses.name: Understanding Today’s News
courses.description: Examines news institutions, editorial decisions, press responsibilities and the economic, political and global forces affecting journalism.

category_review.locator: JRNL 1150 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course examines media institutions, press freedom, economics, politics, diversity and news decisions across societies.

courses.name: The First Amendment and the Media
courses.description: Examines tensions between private rights and public information needs in media law.

category_review.locator: JRNL 3550 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Libel, privacy, government-information access and competing public/private rights establish legal and ethical analysis.

courses.name: Ethics and Diversity in the News Media
courses.description: Examines journalistic ethics, professional standards and diversity through current news and a substantial analytical paper.

category_review.locator: JRNL 4650 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: News-media responsibilities, professional ethical principles and diversity are examined through current reporting and a major ethical-analysis paper.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering

category_review.locator: MATH 1341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

courses.name: Issues in Race, Science, and Technology
courses.description: Examines how scientific and technological changes affect racialized communities and social inequality.

category_review.locator: AFCS 2600 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description examines social and racial impacts of computing, biological and physical technologies on communities; it does not teach those technologies as a technical curriculum.

courses.name: Cyberlaw: Privacy, Ethics, and Digital Rights

category_review.locator: CY 5240 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course studies law, privacy, rights and criminal misuse surrounding information security rather than technical security mechanisms.

courses.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
courses.description: Examines how digital technologies shape knowledge and evaluates their effects through ethics and epistemology.

category_review.locator: DS 1300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Ethics and epistemology evaluate the societal effects of information technologies and policies; technology examples do not make this an AI-methods course.

courses.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
courses.description: Examines digital technology’s effects on knowledge through ethics and epistemology.

category_review.locator: PHIL 1300 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Epistemological and ethical frameworks evaluate information technologies and policies; mentioning machine learning does not establish AI-method instruction.

courses.name: History of Technology

category_review.locator: HIST 2220 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies the global historical development and circulation of science and technology in society, culture and ethics.

courses.name: Data Storytelling
courses.description: Develops data-journalism projects using analysis, visualization and tools for communicating quantitative evidence.

category_review.locator: JRNL 3700 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course explicitly emphasizes journalistic storytelling for broad public audiences, using quantitative analysis and visualization tools in service of communication.

courses.name: Technology and Human Values
courses.description: Examines technology’s social dimensions and ethical implications.

category_review.locator: PHIL 1145 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies philosophy and ethics of technology, human relationships with technology and its social dimensions.

courses.name: The Twenty-First-Century Workplace

category_review.locator: SOCL 1280 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course examines organization, labor control, workplace culture, inequalities and technological change through historical and social analysis.

category_review.rationale: The course analyzes social/political contexts of technological change and institutional responses to the internet and AI; technologies are objects of social analysis, not AI implementation methods.

courses.name: First-Year Writing
courses.description: Develops research and writing across audiences and genres through workshop practice.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1111 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The workshop teaches rhetorical choices, research-based writing, audience awareness and revision in academic, professional and public communication.

courses.name: Coding for Digital Storytelling

category_review.locator: JRNL 5500 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Unlike storytelling courses that merely use applications, this description explicitly centers on coding and basic web development, Python, JavaScript, APIs and reverse engineering software-based projects.

notes: Credits use the catalog’s stated semester hours. Bundle credits belong to requirement nodes; individual amounts are supplied only when independently stated by a course catalog. Unverified alternative-course amounts and variable-credit scalar amounts remain unknown.
Course categories are editorial. Source-stated outcomes are paraphrased program aims, not measured graduate outcomes.
The local curriculum is represented; the degree remains partial because full universitywide and conditional policy execution has not been established.

Official subject-catalog metadata checked for 18 courses; each course cites that source. Variable subject-catalog credit ranges remain null in scalar credits, while program-specific required credits remain on their requirement nodes.

Universitywide and NUpath criteria are now represented through verified shared policy bindings. The major-page reference notes describe what that page incorporates; linked policy rules appear separately in the resolved graph.

Open subject/level ranges, explicit grade/overlap limits and advisor-approved substitutions are represented criteria, not missing invented finite course lists. Individual approvals and registration eligibility remain governed by those rules.

NUpath is competency-based: approved attributes may be met through major or elective courses. This inventory does not fabricate all eligible class sections. BA-language, NYC-campus and nursing-specific general-education panels are not inherited by these Boston BS/BSEnvE degrees.

Permitted home-college options and their additional progression/graduation rules have not been exhaustively verified for this combined degree. Catalog hosting context is not assumed to fix the student’s designated home college.
